name: ESIN entry points for the pediatric radius
aliases: elastic stable intramedullary nailing radius entry (child)
corridor: Distal radial metaphyseal entry 1–1.5 cm proximal to the physis, either laterally between the first and second compartments or dorsally in line with Lister's tubercle, for retrograde elastic nailing

positioning.text: Position supine with the arm on a hand table and image intensifier available to localize the entry relative to the distal radial physis.

surface_landmarks.text: Identify the distal radial physis, the radial styloid, and Lister's tubercle; the entry sits 1 to 1.5 cm proximal to the growth plate.

incision.text: For a lateral entry, incise at the entry level and extend about 2 cm distally (or 3–4 cm proximal to the joint if no imaging); for a Lister's tubercle entry, use a transverse skin-crease incision for cosmesis.

superficial_interval.text: Spread bluntly to bone; for the lateral entry stay anterior to the first compartment and protect the superficial radial nerve, cephalic vein, and thumb tendons.

deep_interval.text: Open a small cortical window in the metaphysis proximal to the physis; for a dorsal entry stay proximal to Lister's tubercle because its tip is part of the epiphysis.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with superficial radial nerve branches, extensor tendon compartments, and the distal radial metaphyseal cortex.

structures_at_risk.text: The superficial radial nerve, cephalic vein, and thumb extensor/abductor tendons are at risk with the lateral entry, and the distal radial physis is at risk with any entry, particularly at Lister's tubercle.

danger_zones.text: The tip of Lister's tubercle is part of the epiphysis; do not open the bone there because it will injure the growth plate.

retraction_hazards.text: Keep superficial radial nerve branches and the cephalic vein out of the retractor, and avoid levering against the physis.

exposure.text: Exposes a small metaphyseal cortical window sufficient to introduce an elastic nail while sparing the physis.

limitations.text: The window gives no direct fracture visualization and relies on closed reduction and imaging; without imaging a more proximal entry is safer.

indications.text: Indicated to establish a physeal-sparing distal radial entry for elastic stable intramedullary nailing in children.

closure.text: Trim and bury the nail end to limit skin irritation, and close subcutaneous tissue and skin.

complications.text: Complications include superficial radial nerve injury, physeal injury with growth disturbance, and skin irritation or bursitis over the nail end.

procedure_applications.condition: A pediatric both-bone or radial shaft fracture is treated with elastic stable intramedullary nailing

questions.question: How far proximal to the physis is the pediatric radial ESIN entry placed?
questions.answer: About 1 to 1.5 cm proximal to the growth plate.

questions.question: Why must the surgeon avoid opening bone at the tip of Lister's tubercle in a child?
questions.answer: Because the tip is part of the epiphysis and opening it injures the growth plate.

questions.question: Which nerve is most at risk with the lateral radial entry?
